title: Demand Cartographer and Fallback Orchestration Playbook
creator: Priya Desai
description:
Problem statement:
Teams encounter unpredictable model supply and regional latency spikes. Current fallback rules are ad-hoc and siloed between Platform, Routing, and Procurement. We need a repeatable product playbook that maps demand signals (customer cohorts, latency patterns, token-cost elasticity) to procurement triggers and automated fallback policies that degrade gracefully while preserving SLAs and unit economics.

Goal:
Create a Demand Cartographer artifact and an associated operational playbook that: (1) synthesizes competitive and marketplace signals into scored procurement triggers; (2) defines deterministic fallback orchestration rules that can be implemented by Routing/Runtime; (3) supplies PM/ProdOps with an experiment slate and runbook to validate thresholds in production. The output should be a concise decision canvas plus a prioritized action backlog for Dedicated and Hosted tiers.
acceptance_criteria: Cartographer matrix: maps 6 demand signal dimensions -> procurement trigger scores (latency, price elasticity, model fragility, regional availability, enterprise SLA, feature-compatibility)
Fallback rules: 3 deterministic policy templates documented (latency-first, cost-first, fidelity-first) with explicit routing precedence and percent thresholds
Operational playbook: runbook for triggering procurement conversations and reserved capacity sizing when trigger score >= 0.7
Experiment slate: 4 field experiments defined (A/B canary, regional throttles, synthetic workload ramp, quantized fallback) with success metrics
Telemetry hooks documented: signal names, dashboard widgets, synthetic workload generator links, and alert thresholds
updates: 2025-11-07 - Created ticket. Initial owner and scope outlined with ProdEng and Platform leads.
2025-11-09 - Scoping workshop with routing, procurement, and research; agreed on 6 signal dimensions and preliminary weighting heuristic.
2025-11-10 - Decided to prioritize 'latency-first' template for Q1 pilot in NA region. Miguel to draft policy YAML for Routing team.
Action items: Miguel - draft policy templates by 2025-11-20; Research - deliver competitive availability ledger by 2025-11-24; ProdOps - add synthetic workload generator to staging by 2025-12-05.
risks_and_assumptions: Assume procurement lead time of 6-10 weeks for Dedicated capacity in constrained regions
Risk: model provider API contract changes could invalidate compatibility scoring; plan a weekly ingestion job
Assume telemetry spike noise during rollout; experiments must include noise-resilient metrics
implementation_notes: Use existing routing precedence mechanism; extend to accept 'trigger_score' metadata from Cartographer service
Quantization fallback variants should be surfaced as model-compatible options in the catalog with cost/latency deltas
Telemetry: add signal names as 'cartographer.*' and expose 90th/99th percentile derivatives for alerting
next_steps: Finalize scoring rubric and weights with Research (deadline 2025-11-24)
Produce policy templates and YAML examples for Routing (deadline 2025-11-20)
Schedule field experiment kickoff with ProdOps and Sales pilot customers (target 2025-12-08)
Create dashboard mockups for cartographer signals and procurement triggers (owner: Sara Kim, by 2025-11-30)
